data.title: Drag
data.tagline: Move or reorder an item by holding and pulling it
data.description: Drag interaction works for rearranging cards, moving files, and choosing a range. Show what can be grabbed, where it may be dropped, and the result before release. Provide another method for people who cannot or do not want to drag.

use: Place an object on a canvas
Adjust a continuous value with a handle
avoid: Make dragging the only way to complete an important task
Start a drag when the user intended to scroll
Move an item without confirming its new position

lessonPractice.title: Task cards support drag reordering, but keyboard users and people with unsteady movement must also change the order. Which design is complete?

options.label: Support dragging only and use a stronger shadow to confirm pickup
options.feedback: The shadow explains drag state but provides no way to reorder for someone who cannot drag reliably.

options.label: Show a drag handle and drop position, plus Move up and Move down actions
options.feedback: Drag feedback clarifies the gesture, while alternative actions let keyboard and motor-impaired users complete the same task.

options.label: Make the whole card draggable and disable text selection and normal clicks
options.feedback: A full-card drag target conflicts with selecting text and using links, and it still lacks keyboard reordering.

data.agentPrompt: Improve task reordering with a clear drag handle, picked-up state, and drop placeholder, plus Move up and Move down actions. Do not make the whole card a drag target. Reorder the same card with mouse, touch, and keyboard and verify the final order.

references.title: Drag-and-Drop: How to Design for Ease of Use
